items.title: GAMING: A business case for a ‘butt slider’ in Final Fantasy XIV
items.summary: Final Fantasy XIV’s next challenge isn’t finding new players. It’s keeping the millions who already love it, as Harrison Polites explains.
items.content:
Facebook X LinkedIn Bluesky Copy to Clipboard Copy Gaming

Prefer Startup Daily Wuk Lamat with Y’stola Rhul, one of Final Fantasy XIV’s most famous Miqo’te characters. Source: Square Enix. There was a telling moment buried in director Naoki Yoshida’s two-hour keynote kicking off Berlin’s Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival last weekend. For years, and despite player requests, Final Fantasy XIV forced players who chose the popular cat-people race, the Miqo’te, to wear tribal tattoos on their face as a matter of lore. In the coming expansion, Evercold, and its patches to follow, that will become an option.

Sandwiched between calls from the audience and jostling from his translator Koji Fox to introduce a “butt slider” — a tool to adjust the size of your avatar’s derriere — Yoshida conceded he had initially been opposed to the tattoo change. But it’s happening anyway. It was a small but important admission, and one that speaks to the broader state of Final Fantasy XIV and its parent company Square Enix.

Since reaching its peak around the Endwalker expansion in late 2021 — when Square Enix suspended digital sales of the game outright because its servers couldn’t absorb the demand — Final Fantasy XIV has been Square Enix’s golden goose.

Its Massively Multiplayer Online (MMO) division, which includes both Final Fantasy XIV and Dragon Quest X, is one of the company’s most profitable. Square refuses to separate the two in its reporting, but Final Fantasy XIV is much larger. Put plainly: last year it out-earned Square Enix’s entire blockbuster console and PC games business.

There’s concern from Square Enix’s investors and industry analysts that this is actually a problem. The games research firm Naavik put it bluntly earlier this year: the company risks leaning on declining free-to-play and MMO revenues to subsidise increasingly ambitious AAA launches.

By continuing, you agree to our Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy .

The most pertinent example is Final Fantasy VII Rebirth. It was, by any critical measure, a triumph. It also missed Square Enix’s internal expectations — and when chief executive Takashi Kiryu conceded to analysts that recent big-budget releases had underperformed, Square Enix shares fell 16% , their steepest single-day drop in 13 years.

Meanwhile Final Fantasy XIV, while still going strong, has moved backwards.

Square Enix doesn’t publish subscriber figures, so the best available proxy is the long-running Lodestone census maintained by the Japanese site Lucky Bancho, which tracks active characters. It recorded around 1.22 million in June 2024, immediately before Dawntrail. It’s latest July 2026 census recorded 950,000 active players.

The financials say the same thing in a different dialect . In the quarter ending June 2025, MMO sales fell 23% year on year and operating profit fell 45%.

The party line, repeated at almost every event, is that fan feedback is paramount to the game’s longevity and that the team follows it to the letter. But from a veteran player’s perspective, it felt as if development resources were spent courting new players rather than catering to existing ones.

Significant effort went into retrofitting old content so it could be undertaken solo: an on-ramp for players who might enjoy Final Fantasy’s universe but bounce off the MMO aspects of it. The same goes for the graphical overhaul. Nobody will dispute the results — the game has never looked better — but enfranchised players were used to the aesthetics they had, and the dated look was, arguably, only ever a problem for incoming players.

The challenge is that even with updates and tweaks and a generous extended free trial, it is incredibly difficult to convince new players to pick up Final Fantasy XIV. Believe me, I’ve tried.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV launches a free trial on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: The most popular MMORPG finally arrives to Nintendo SWitch 2, and you can try it for free.
items.content:
The gates to Eorzea have officially opened on Nintendo Switch 2, and this time, you don't need to buy a ticket. Square Enix has launched the Final Fantasy XIV Free Trial on the new console, giving curious adventurers the chance to experience one of the world's most successful MMORPGs without paying a subscription or worrying about a time limit.

Calling it a "trial" almost feels misleading. Rather than offering a brief taste of the game, the free version includes the entirety of A Realm Reborn and the first three expansions— Heavensward , Stormblood , and Shadowbringers . New players can journey through an enormous story spanning hundreds of quests, challenge iconic bosses, clear dungeons and raids, and experiment with every available combat, crafting, and gathering job up to level 80. It's enough content to keep most RPG fans occupied for months.

One of Final Fantasy XIV's biggest strengths is its flexibility. A single character can learn every class in the game, allowing players to swap between roles whenever they like instead of creating multiple characters. Whether you prefer charging into battle as a tank, keeping allies alive as a healer, dealing massive damage, or taking a break to become Eorzea's finest blacksmith or fisherman, the Free Trial lets you experience nearly every side of the game.

As generous as it is, the trial isn't completely unrestricted. Free accounts cannot use the Market Board, trade items with other players, create parties or Free Companies, send direct messages, or participate in PvP modes. There's also a cap of 300,000 gil, ensuring the trial remains focused on exploration and story rather than the game's player-driven economy.

There's one important detail for newcomers: the Free Trial is only available for new service accounts. Once an account purchases the full game, it permanently transitions to the standard version, which requires a monthly subscription after the included game time expires. For that reason, players may want to squeeze every last dungeon, raid, and side quest out of the trial before making the jump.

Switch 2 owners should also make sure they have plenty of room to spare. Final Fantasy XIV requires around 117 GB of free storage, making it one of the largest downloads currently available on Nintendo's latest console. On the bright side, there's no need for a Nintendo Switch Online membership to play, so once the game is installed, the only thing standing between you and your next adventure is deciding which job to level first.

For anyone who's been waiting for the right moment to see what all the excitement is about, this might be it. With four complete chapters of the saga available at no cost, the Switch 2 Free Trial offers an adventure that's less of a demo and more of a full-blown fantasy epic. 0 Square Enix is bringing Final Fantasy XIV to Switch 2 today! The game will require a subscription fee (as it does on other platforms), but Switch Online won’t be necessary to play. You can see all the details below, and please note that you’ll need 117GB to downoad this one.

To celebrate the game’s release on Nintendo Switch 2, both versions of the Complete Edition are 30% off until Thursday, 13 August 2026!

To help ensure a stable launch experience, subscription fees will be waived for approximately one month following release.

Following this period, the 30-day free play period included when registering a new platform will begin. Once this time has elapsed, a subscription fee will be required to continue playing. A separate subscription is required to play the Nintendo Switch 2 version, regardless of whether you are subscribed on another platform. However, if you have remaining game time on other platforms, the Nintendo Switch 2 subscription will be available at half price.

(Please note that the half price discount is not available while free game time is active on other platforms.)

A subscription to Nintendo Switch Online is not required to play FINAL FANTASY XIV.

A Square Enix account and Nintendo account are required to play FINAL FANTASY XIV.

Upon launching for the very first time, the Nintendo Switch 2 user profile will be linked to your Square Enix account. You will not be able to unlink the accounts or transfer to another account once linked. Please be careful and confirm that both accounts are correct before linking.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV on Switch 2 is Better Than Anyone Expected
items.summary: Final Fantasy XIV is shaping up to be one of the Switch 2's most technically ambitious ports, with Square Enix targeting stable performance while bringing the full MMORPG experience to Nintendo's latest hybrid console.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV is shaping up to be one of the Switch 2's most technically ambitious ports, with Square Enix targeting stable performance while bringing the full MMORPG experience to Nintendo's latest hybrid console.

When Final Fantasy XIV was first announced for Nintendo Switch 2, skepticism was understandable. This is, after all, an MMORPG that has been evolving continuously for more than a decade. It spans multiple expansions, supports hundreds of players in shared social spaces, features massive raids, sprawling cities, and some of the busiest online hubs in gaming.

Translating all of that to a handheld system seemed like an enormous technical challenge. But it's clear that Square Enix seems to be taking on the task very seriously based on our early impressions of the game so far today at launch.

Producer and director Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P) has confirmed that the team has prioritized consistent performance over raw frame rate, targeting a stable 30 FPS throughout the majority of gameplay . Rather than chasing higher numbers, the focus has been on maintaining smooth combat and reliable frame pacing during the content players spend most of their time enjoying things like main scenario quests, dungeons, trials, raids, crafting, gathering, and exploration.

"I want to be honest with you: we are working really hard on the optimisation. We are striving to get the best performance. I think with the towns, you may see a lower framerate, only because there are so many players that are rendered on the screen.

The Nintendo Switch 2 is a wonderful console, and I think you can choose the way you want to play. You are more free to choose which mode to play in, so I hope that players will find the way to play that is most suited for themselves."

- Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P), game director, during a press conference

Cities like Limsa Lominsa regularly fill with hundreds of player characters showing off mounts, glamour sets, minions, and particle-heavy abilities. Even on significantly more powerful hardware, those areas have historically been among the game's toughest rendering scenarios. Square Enix has been transparent that these locations are where Switch 2 players are most likely to see performance fluctuate, but the team says it has spent considerable time optimizing the experience leading up to launch.

From the time I've spent with the game so far, you can definitely feel the impact. But since these are social gathering areas or just dialogue- and menu-heavy environments, it's not really a big detractor from gameplay. When you're outside of the city doing quests or in an instance, it's been very smooth so far.

I picked up playing with my level 30 Gladiator I abandoned a few years ago on PC, so it's been a little bit of a learning curve so far. Fortunately, if you really want to, you don't have to play in handheld mode or using a controller since there's mouse support on Switch 2, including both USB options and the Joy-Con's mouse mode.

"As everyone already knows, the Nintendo Switch 2 is an amazing piece of hardware. If you place it in the dock, you can play in TV mode. If you use it in Portable mode, you can carry it and play it at your leisure. For example, when challenging a high-difficulty Raid, you can play on TV while connecting a mouse and keyboard, and then you can craft and gather while in Portable mode. I feel like this will enable a play style that is unique to Nintendo Switch 2.

Following the announcement at the keynote speech, I also saw some voices on social media asking, 'Is it going to be alright spec-wise?', but we are thoroughly optimizing it. There are no performance issues at all during actual content. It's much more hectic when you're in a town with a lot of characters, though I think it should run stably around 30 frames there as well. The performance is better in the actual content, so I think it should be okay, and you should not worry."

- Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P), game director, in an interview with Famitsu reported by RPGSite

Unlike many MMORPG adaptations, this isn't a separate handheld version with isolated servers or reduced functionality. Switch 2 players log into the same persistent world as everyone else across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. Every expansion, every raid, every social space, every seasonal event, and every update arrives together, allowing players to seamlessly continue their existing characters wherever they choose to play in both handheld and docked modes.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV is finally available on Switch 2, Complete Edition 30% off for next few days
items.summary: After announcing it earlier this year, Square Enix has finally released Final Fantasy XIV on the Nintendo Switch 2. Available in its “Free Trial,” “Starter
items.content:
After announcing it earlier this year , Square Enix has finally released Final Fantasy XIV on the Nintendo Switch 2. Available in its “Free Trial,” “Starter Edition,” and “Complete Edition” formats, players can now journey across the land of Hydaelyn from the comfort of their hybrid console. Playing an MMO from the toilet does sound like an interesting way to pass the time while doing your business, in-game and out.

To commemorate the occasion, the “Complete Edition” is currently 30% off on the eShop for the next few days. Including 30 days of game access as well as every expansion (of which there are six), you can grab it for $41.99 until August 8th, 2026. The “Starter Edition,” meanwhile, will run you $20 and includes the base game with its four expansions and 30 days of game access. The “Free Trial,” meanwhile, is probably the better option for people unfamiliar with MMOs.

Unlike other trials for MMOs, Final Fantasy XIV’s Free Trial is actually ludicrously generous. Granting access to the full campaign and its first three expansions, the only real restrictions involve interacting with other players. You cannot use the Party Finder, cannot chat, can’t register friends, cannot trade, and cannot buy houses. You’re also capped to level 80 and only able to access 18 of the 22 available jobs, though you can still experience the main story of Final Fantasy XIV. Think of it more like an extended demo rather than a sampler.

The game will take up a whopping 117 GB on your Switch 2, but if you’re a Final Fantasy faithful, then that’s probably worth it. I might give the trial a shot since playing something like an MMO on a portable device is still pretty novel.

items.content:
The Make It Rain Campaign returns once more to the Gold Saucer! With a 50% MGP bonus and an assortment of adorable otter-themed goods on offer, you won't want to miss out! Furthermore, campaign attendants will be offering a range of items at discounted prices, including some exclusive limited-time deals, so be sure to join the festivities and rake in the rewards while you can!

Event Duration

From Friday, May 29, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9:00 (BST) / 18:00 (AEST) to Wednesday, June 24, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / 15:59 (BST) / Thursday, 25 June at 0:59 (AEST)

How to Participate

Begin the quest "You Otter Be There" by speaking to Ollier in Ul’dah - Steps of Nald (X:9.4 Y:9.1). * Players must be level 15 and above to start the quest. * Players must first complete the quest "It Could Happen to You."

Rewards

* MGP rewards from the Gold Saucer have been increased by 50% for the duration of this event. * Certain items available during previous iterations of the event can be obtained via the campaign attendant. * The Crystal Tower striker, Monster Toss machine, Cuff-a-Cur machine, and a number of other prizes may be purchased at a reduced MGP cost from the campaign attendant. Visit the special site for more details.
